task_spec: SUBJECT: A NiceGUI Phase 1 'reconnect wizard' - a guided GUI workflow that finds Traktor collection tracks whose files have moved, lets an operator review the proposed matches as objects mid-run, and writes the repaired .nml. This is section 5 sequencing step 4 of docs/nicegui-gui-analysis.md; steps 1-3 (parity manifest, renderer split, on_progress/cancel) are committed.
scope: new traktor_nml/gui/ package; new tests under tests/
scope: exactly two subcommands, the only ones marked Phase 1 in section 1's Tier 1 table - scan-reconnect-candidates and rewrite-from-reconnect
out-of-scope: the Tier 2 generated-form machinery (section 4) - separate work, though scan-reconnect-candidates is also Tier 2 eligible
out-of-scope: Tier 1 Phase 2 (preview-diff, rewrite) and Phase 3 (build-playlist, discover-tracks, discover-collection-tracks)
out-of-scope: Tier 3 entirely (splice, split, rewrite-from-collection-compare) - deliberately excluded, needs a different review UI
out-of-scope: section 6 packaging and section 7 hosting - the spike already ran and passed (docs/2026-08-25-packaging-spike-results.md)
out-of-scope: any change to matching, refutation or the confidence ladder
constraints: MUST NOT: modify tests/baselines/manifest.json. Non-regeneration IS the parity check.
MUST NOT: change PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256 in tests/test_parity_baseline.py.
MUST: stdout, stderr, exit codes and written output bytes stay byte-identical for every existing CLI command. Typed errors keep exit code 2.
MUST NOT: any import from traktor_nml/gui/ in traktor_nml/commands/ or traktor_nml/cli.py. Enforced by tests/test_gui_import_isolation.py.
MUST NOT: any top-level nicegui import reachable from commands/__init__.py, which imports every command module at CLI startup, before argv is parsed. Enforced by tests/test_cli_without_nicegui.py.
MUST: nicegui stays an optional extra. pyproject.toml declares gui = ['nicegui>=3.16.0'].
MUST: every new subcommand stays classified. tests/test_gui_command_classification.py asserts total-and-disjoint tiers plus the closed side-effect allowlist.

MUST: full suite stays at or above 243 passed, at most 3 skipped. The 3 skips are the fingerprint tier (pyacoustid/fpcalc absent) and are expected. A silently lost or newly skipped test fails this as surely as a red one; read counts off the pytest summary line.

MUST: every new guard test constructs its broken scenario in executable code and demonstrates the divergence; the docstring records the specific mutation and the specific observed output. 'A guard you have only seen pass is not a guard.'
MUST NOT: claim proof not actually run. An over-correction claiming unearned proof was itself flagged as a defect during this project's review.

MUST: documentation describes the code as it stands - no 'previously', 'used to', 'now does', 'no longer', 'as before', 'gains', 'moves', 'added'. Largest finding category across this project (seven instances).
MUST NOT: restore a file with git checkout. An agent did that here, destroyed uncommitted work, and rebuilt from a spec. Copy aside and restore from the copy.
MUST NOT: delete or write into build/ or dist/ - untracked PyInstaller spike bundles. Three agents have written there this session; one destroyed them.
SHOULD: run.io_bound for the disk scan, not run.cpu_bound - cpu_bound uses a process pool and TagCache/lxml roots are not cleanly picklable.
entry_points: traktor_nml/reconnect_run.py:run_reconnection(args, old_root, *, on_progress=None, cancel=None, diagnostics=None) -> ReconnectResult - the printless pipeline the GUI drives
traktor_nml/reconnect_run.py:scan_reconnect_candidates / rewrite_from_reconnect - the two Phase 1 cores, both taking on_progress/cancel
traktor_nml/reconnect_run.py:ReconnectResult - frozen dataclass carrying mapping, stats, ambiguity_rows, old_records, warnings, diagnostics. The review table reads this directly.
traktor_nml/reconnect_run.py:ScanReconnectResult / RewriteReconnectResult - typed per-command results carrying error, csv_path, outcome, diagnostics

traktor_nml/reconnect_render.py:render_scan_reconnect_candidates / render_rewrite_from_reconnect / emit - CLI rendering; the GUI must NOT route through emit, but the key=value lines it produces are what ui.log should show
traktor_nml/rewrite.py:plan_and_write_nml -> WriteOutcome - printless write shell; write_nml_safely is the printing wrapper
traktor_nml/diskscan.py:index_scan_roots(..., on_progress, cancel, on_diagnostic) - all three default None and inert
spike/packaging/spike_app.py - the spike's NiceGUI app, a working reference for nicegui in this repo
rejected_alternatives: Subprocess-scraping the CLI key=value stdout as the GUI data source - Tier 1 needs structured data mid-run for live progress and an interactive ambiguous-match table; a parsed transcript exists only once the run is over. Survives only as the section 5 fallback.
nicegui.run.cpu_bound for the scan - process pool, and TagCache/lxml roots are not cleanly picklable.
ui.upload for scan roots - a browser upload; scan roots must live on the server's filesystem.
Placing GUI code under traktor_nml/commands/ - commands/__init__.py imports every command module at CLI startup.
current_understanding: The reconnect path already runs in three layers: reconnect_run.py owns the pipeline and returns objects, reconnect_render.py owns every character reaching a stream, commands/reconnect_cmd.py owns only argparse. That split exists specifically so a GUI can sit beside the CLI renderer.
on_progress and cancel already thread from both cores through run_reconnection into index_scan_roots, defaulting to None so the CLI path is unchanged.
traktor_nml/gui/ does not exist yet. Both isolation guards and the classification guard were written against a tree without it, deliberately, so they hold a clean baseline.
The parity manifest holds 12 cases; all 12 recorded stderr values are empty, which makes asserting stderr a leak detector for any stream write escaping the renderer.
The packaging spike passed on Windows: lxml and fpcalc both bundle correctly under PyInstaller --onedir with nicegui 3.16.0.
assumptions: The GUI drives the cores directly and does NOT call reconnect_render.emit; it renders its own view from the result objects (H)
ui.log should show the same key=value vocabulary the CLI prints, which means the renderer's line-producing functions are reusable without emit (M - needs checking that they are separable from emit)
nicegui is installed in .venv already (the spike used it), so development can proceed without new environment work (H)

No pytest plugin for driving NiceGUI is present; section 3.3's acceptance criteria are expressed against the cores and the write path rather than against rendered DOM, so they are testable without a browser harness (M)
invisible_knowledge: The single strongest property in the plan (section 3.3): taking a preview result, applying ZERO operator overrides, and writing must produce a file byte-identical to the equivalent non-dry-run CLI invocation. It proves the review layer cannot silently change outcomes and is checkable against manifest bytes directly.
Preview must write zero bytes anywhere except the documented tag-cache exception. Test by snapshotting every file's mtime and size under tmp_path; only .traktor_nml_tagcache.json may differ.
The tag cache and the ambiguity CSV are written even under --dry-run, because neither is the command's declared output.

The output-collision refusal (output_must_differ_from_input) is the FIRST thing plan_and_write_nml does, ahead of parsing and ahead of the caller's callback, so a refused write never costs a 20-minute scan. It must surface as a typed refusal the GUI renders as a disabled button with a reason - not an exit code.

A cancelled scan raises ScanCancelled and yields NO result at all, because a short candidate list is indistinguishable from a complete one and would report most of the collection as missing. Nothing on the core or write path catches it.
Volume identities are resolved once per run and reused by the fingerprint tier and the LOCATION re-encoding.

stderr order is scan diagnostics, then the fingerprint dependency warning, then the refutation-disabled line, then any error. stdout order for rewrite-from-reconnect is csv_written, then the stats/sample_matches block, then output_written.

File selection is the known friction point and the piece most likely to feel clumsy. NiceGUI has no server-side file picker. In native mode call pywebview's create_file_dialog; otherwise NiceGUI's local_file_picker example component. Section 4 says to budget for it.
A full scan against the real corpus takes about 20 minutes, so verification runs on the fixture corpus.

Section 1's prose is internally contradictory about 'exactly one tier list' vs scan-reconnect-candidates appearing in two; tests/test_gui_command_classification.py encodes the resolution as two predicates and records the contradiction.

This repo's decision log is DL-001..DL-057 in traktor_nml/README.md. A DL tag marks the decision a statement traces to and the statement lives in whichever section describes it; each decision is stated once, so a second copy would drift.
Keep timestamped-backup convention the repo already uses (*.pre_playlist_inspection_<ts>.nml) and put ui.dialog before writes.
